A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RAGGED research, with matching authors, core experiments and retained results. All 12 pages of v2 and 17 pages of v3, including appendices, figures, tables and equations, support comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original retrieval and reader experiments on Natural Questions, HotpotQA and BioASQ, including context-depth curves and gold/no-gold analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds CRAG results, further model comparisons, diagnostic scores and prompting/reranking experiments.

M1.justification: The underlying retrieve-top-k-and-read procedure and decoding remain unchanged. The new diagnostic metrics and tested reranking/prompt configurations extend evaluation; v3 does not introduce a new proposed reader architecture, training objective or core generation algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 adds a preliminary CRAG evaluation using FLAN T5 and LLAMA2 (Appendix F, Table 6). Natural Questions, HotpotQA and BioASQ remain. This is a limited coverage extension; the PDFs do not specify which CRAG domains or subsets were evaluated.

E2.justification: v3 adds Contriever to retrieval comparisons and evaluates it against ColBERT with FLAN T5 and LLAMA2 7B (Figure 15, Table 9). It also adds GPT-4o versus GPT-3.5 on NQ (Figure 16), plus base, relevance-prompt, reranked and combined configurations (Figures 8, 17–18), substantially broadening the comparisons.

E3.justification: v3 introduces RSS/RSC evaluation with specified window and gain-threshold parameters, Prometheus semantic scoring on an NQ subset, and controlled prompting/reranking comparisons. CRAG adds a separate retrieval-depth evaluation. The original datasets' reported sizes, F1/recall metrics and decoding settings remain; these additions do not establish that the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Alongside the retained gold/no-gold analyses, v3 adds tests of prompting and reranking effects, semantic-metric validation, RSS/RSC hyperparameter sensitivity, and whether input truncation explains FLAN T5's stability (Sections 2 and 6.3; Appendices G, J and O). These address several additional robustness and measurement questions.

E5.justification: v3 Section 2 newly reports F1 standard-deviation summaries, with mean 0.38 and maximum 0.46, to justify the RSC threshold. The variability source and repeated-run counts are not specified, so this is additional variability reporting, not evidence of increased runs or seed-based uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v3 adds RSS/RSC scores, CRAG outcomes, Contriever and GPT-4o results, semantic scores, intervention curves and numerical summary tables. Existing BM25/ColBERT recall values match v2 Table 3 and v3 Table 9. The retriever discussion changes from k=5 examples to across-depth and optimal-performance summaries, so its changed gain figures are not same-setting performance changes. v3 also omits several comparative accuracies from v2's no-gold/same-Wikipedia-page subgroup discussion.

T1.justification: v3 Section 2 adds substantive mathematical definitions: RSS measures the minimum nearby performance relative to peak performance, and RSC uses a trapezoidal performance aggregate with a gain-threshold stopping criterion. These central formal definitions are absent from v2; no accompanying theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The two reader-response patterns remain, but v3 recasts the contribution around quantitative stability and scalability diagnostics. Its abstract, introduction and conclusion additionally claim that retriever, reranker and prompting choices do not fundamentally alter reader-driven trends, expanding the scope beyond v2's configuration guidance.

C2.justification: v3 adds training-based explanations for reader behavior, hypotheses about distracting semantic retrieval, and domain-dependent explanations for prompting/reranking effects. It also discusses RSS asymmetry and the distinction between stability and scalability. Conversely, v2's explicit limitations concerning task, model, language and domain generalizability are not retained.

D1.justification: v3 documents the exact relevance-focused instruction, Prometheus-7b-v2.0 and its five-point scoring scale, and RSS/RSC parameter choices. Existing hardware, token limits, decoding settings and code/data access information remain. The added reranker and CRAG evaluation are not fully specified.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion is substantially refocused around retrieval-depth disagreements, domain effects and retriever-reader interactions. v3 adds works including Cuconasu, Jiang, Finardi and Kandpal, plus references for Contriever, Prometheus and CRAG, while removing much of v2's context-filtering and long-context literature. It newly emphasizes realistic retrieval versus oracle-curated evaluation as a distinguishing feature.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, framework description and conclusion are extensively rewritten around stability and scalability. The no-context comparison becomes a standalone research question, experimental setup is consolidated, and v2's recurring analysis guidelines are replaced by question-led discussion and key takeaways. Appendices are substantially reorganized.

P2.justification: v3 redraws the framework roadmap, adds a colored configuration-summary table and diagnostic bar charts, and introduces several comparison plots and tables. v2 Figures 3 and 8 are combined in appendix Figure 14, while the gold/no-gold plots are retained across relocation and renumbering. These changes substantially alter the visual organization beyond the conference-template change.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful semantic validation and controlled interventions absent from v2, but new reporting inconsistencies undermine its stronger conclusions. Section 5 claims LLAMA2 degradation on CRAG, whereas Table 6 shows an increase from 0.20 to 0.23 followed by a plateau. Table 1 says LLAMA2 7B with BM25 improves over closed-book NQ performance at every k, while Table 5 reports even its optimal gain as -0.5. These material inconsistencies coexist with the added evidence, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
